verdicts.question: What type of roof is present at the site?
verdicts.photo_observation: Pages 6, 8, 11, 12, 13: flat concrete terrace with weathered dark waterproofing, cement parapet walls and a concrete headroom slab. No tiles or metal sheets seen.
verdicts.rationale: The flat RCC terrace in several roof photos matches 'RCC Flat Roof'.

verdicts.question: Are there any obstructions on the roof that could affect the solar installation?
verdicts.designer_answer: details: The solar water heater, ladder, are the obstructions that could affect the solar installation.
verdicts.photo_observation: Pages 6, 8, 11, 12, 13: an evacuated-tube solar water heater with its tank stands on the terrace. A steel ladder leans on the headroom. Page 13 also shows a glass skylight/roof light on the terrace (blue rectangle in the p23 render) and the headroom block itself.
verdicts.rationale: The water heater and ladder the designer lists are clearly visible. The skylight and headroom are other obstructions that were not listed, but the arrays in the p23 layout avoid them.

verdicts.question: What is the angle of the panels? (in degrees)
verdicts.photo_observation: Pages 23-24: SketchUp renders show elevated arrays at a shallow tilt. No dimension or angle annotation is given, and there are no photos of an existing structure.
verdicts.rationale: The renders cannot show whether the tilt is 7°. The photos show only an unbuilt flat roof.

verdicts.question: On how many roofs at the site are we installing solar?
verdicts.photo_observation: Page 23 top view and p24 renders: one 6-panel elevated array and one 2-panel elevated array, both on the parapets/edges of the same main terrace. The p11 'Proposed PV Area' photos mark the same terrace.
verdicts.rationale: Both arrays sit on the one main terrace, so '1' roof is consistent. The arrays are split into two blocks.

verdicts.question: What type of mounting structure is planned?
verdicts.photo_observation: Pages 23-24: renders show the panels raised on MS/AL legs, cantilevered over the parapet walls. The roof surface underneath stays clear (water heater and skylight below).
verdicts.rationale: The elevated structure in the renders matches 'Elevated - AL Short Rail Elevated Structure'.

verdicts.question: What is the orientation of the solar panels?
verdicts.photo_observation: Page 23 top view: the north arrow points to the top of the plan, and the 6-panel array runs along the top (north) edge. The renders do not clearly show which way the panels tilt.
verdicts.rationale: The north arrow is there, but the renders do not clearly show the direction of tilt, so 'South' cannot be confirmed from the images. The GMap/compass should be checked.

verdicts.question: How can the roof be accessed?
verdicts.photo_observation: Page 7 (top) and page 9: an internal granite staircase is captioned as the route for carrying small items. Page 7 (bottom) and page 8 show the staircase arriving at a door that opens onto the terrace. The steel ladder on pp. 8, 11 and 19 only reaches the top of the headroom slab. The panels in the renders are on the main terrace, not on the headroom.
verdicts.rationale: The photos show the terrace where panels go is reached by an internal staircase (p7/p9, 'Staircase Details'). A ladder is needed only for the headroom top (LA location). 'Ladder' contradicts the documented access route, so the answer should be 'Staircase' or 'Staircase + Ladder'.

verdicts.question: Is the building currently under construction?
verdicts.photo_observation: Page 5: a finished, painted building with glazed balcony railings, louvered windows and a completed compound gate. Interiors on p7/p14 are finished (granite stairs, AC, washing machine).
verdicts.rationale: There is no exposed brick, scaffolding or unfinished work. The building is complete.

verdicts.question: In an under-construction building, are existing conduit pipes available for AC, DC cables, and earthing?
verdicts.photo_observation: The building is complete (p5). The cable routes on pp. 12-20 are drawn along the walls, parapets and downpipes as surface runs. No embedded conduit openings were seen.
verdicts.rationale: The question is effectively not applicable to a finished building. 'No' agrees with the surface cable routes that were planned.

verdicts.question: What is the height of the building and how many floors does it have?
verdicts.designer_answer: The height of the building is G+2+headroom is approximately 15 meters
verdicts.photo_observation: Page 5 exterior: a ground/stilt level with gate and parking, two upper residential floors with balconies, and a terrace with a railing/headroom on top. That is about 3 storeys plus headroom.
verdicts.rationale: The visible floor count matches G+2+headroom. A height of about 15 m is plausible but a little high for G+2 (typically about 12-13 m to the headroom top).

verdicts.question: Is the site photo matching with the building description?
verdicts.photo_observation: Page 5 exterior and the terrace photos (pp. 6, 8, 11) are consistent with each other and with the p23-24 renders: L-shaped terrace, headroom with ladder, solar water heater, skylight.
verdicts.rationale: The site photos match the building description and the 3D layout.

verdicts.question: Is there an overhead HT line passing within a 10-meter radius of the site?
verdicts.photo_observation: Page 5: a utility pole with a cross-arm and pin insulators stands right next to the building front (about 1-2 m). Several overhead conductors and service cables cross in front of the balconies. The small dark pin insulators look like LT distribution, but the voltage cannot be confirmed from the photo.
verdicts.rationale: Overhead lines are clearly within 10 m. They look like LT, not HT, but this cannot be confirmed visually, and they lie on the material-lifting face (p5). Confirm the line voltage.

verdicts.question: Can the delivery van/truck reach the material unloading point?
verdicts.photo_observation: Page 5: a paved public road runs directly in front of the compound gate. The bottom photo, taken looking down from the terrace, shows the road right at the building front.
verdicts.rationale: There is direct road access to the gate, and the unloading point is at the front of the building.

verdicts.question: Are there any obstacles at the site that could hinder material lifting?
verdicts.designer_answer: details: The existing chajja are the obstacles that could hinder the material lifting.
verdicts.photo_observation: Page 5: the lifting route (blue line) runs up the building face. Projecting chajjas/sunshades and balconies are visible on every floor. The pole and overhead wires are also close to the front face.
verdicts.rationale: The chajjas are visible along the lifting path, which matches the designer's note. The overhead wires and pole near the front face are an extra lifting hazard the designer did not mention.

verdicts.question: Where will the Inverter, DCDB, ACDB, Battery, etc. be located?

verdicts.rationale: The equipment location is on the terrace level next to the headroom/terrace door, as described.

verdicts.question: Is a canopy required for protecting the Inverters/ACDB/DCDB?

verdicts.question: In Main meter panel, is empty space available for solar meter?

verdicts.question: Is there space available to dig DC, AC and LA earth pits?

verdicts.question: What type of Earthing chamber needs to be installed at site? Is it Cement chamber or PVC chamber?

verdicts.rationale: Whether an LA extension is needed or provided cannot be confirmed visually. Check that the headroom LA covers the far 2-panel array.

verdicts.question: In case of elevated structures, is it with or without grouting?

verdicts.rationale: Grouting cannot be seen in the renders or photos.

verdicts.question: Are there any challenges with respect to Installation and Maintenance activities?
verdicts.photo_observation: Pages 23-24: the arrays are cantilevered over the terrace parapet edges, partly overhanging the building edge. Large items are to be lifted up the facade past chajjas and close to overhead lines (p5). Fuse relocation in the meter box is needed (p21).
verdicts.rationale: The photos show several installation and maintenance considerations (edge-overhanging elevated arrays, external lifting near overhead wires, meter box rework). 'No challenges' looks optimistic. A reviewer should confirm.

verdicts.question: Are there any safety risks associated with accessing the roof for installation?
verdicts.photo_observation: The terrace is reached by an internal staircase and has parapet walls (pp. 6-9). The arrays overhang the parapet edge at about the 3rd-floor level (pp. 23-24), and the LA sits on the headroom top, reached only by an open steel ladder (p19).
verdicts.rationale: Access to the terrace itself looks safe. Work at the parapet edge and on the ladder-only headroom is a working-at-height risk that 'No' does not reflect.

verdicts.question: Is space present in rooftop to store the panels?
verdicts.photo_observation: Page 10 'Material Storage': an open flat terrace section beside the solar water heater has room to lay panels flat.
verdicts.rationale: Clear flat terrace space for horizontal storage is visible.

verdicts.question: Is ventilation available in the battery location?

verdicts.question: Is there any trench work to be done to carry the AC cable to the meter location?
verdicts.photo_observation: Pages 14-18, 20: the AC cable (purple) runs from the utility room along walls and downpipes, through a wall hole (p15) to the meter room (p16). Earth (green) and LA (orange) cables run down the facade to the garden pits. No route crosses open ground or paving.
verdicts.rationale: All documented routes are wall-mounted or pass through walls. No trench is shown.

verdicts.question: Is the cable routing in the site photos continuous and consistent across the documented run — from rooftop panels to DCDB to inverter to ACDB to solar meter to main panel — with no orphan ends, no unexplained mid-run size changes, and visible conduit / cable-tie / clipping where the run is exposed?
verdicts.designer_notes: No designer answer for this target — the vision routine verifies it by tracing cables across photos with 'Cable Routing', 'Equipment Location', 'Meter Box' and similar captions on pages 4+.
verdicts.photo_observation: DC (red/green) runs along the parapets from the arrays (pp. 12-13), down the side face to the utility-room window (p17 top), into the inverter (p14/p21). AC (purple) goes inverter → UPS point → down the wall and pipes (p14 bottom, p15 top) → through a wall hole (p15 bottom) → meter room (p16) → main/solar meter (p21). Earthing (green) goes down a downpipe (p17-18) to the AC/DC pits (p22). LA (orange) goes from the headroom (p19) down the side passage (p20) to the LA pit (p22). The p15 bottom and p16 top photos are heavily blurred. Routes are drawn as overlays with no conduit, cable-tie or clipping detail. Cable sizes are stated only in the observations (4 sq mm DC, 6 sq mm AC, 16 sq mm AL earth, 25x3 GI LA).
verdicts.rationale: The routes can be traced end-to-end with no orphan ends. However, two key photos (pp. 15-16) are too blurry to confirm the wall-hole and meter-room segments, and no conduit or clipping method is shown on exposed runs.
